# Experiment 2 {.unnumbered}

@tbl-supp-exp2 compares separate and joint MinT reconciliation with the base forecasts in Experiment 2.
In every scenario, reconciliation reduces MSE by `r num$suppArimaVsBaseRange`% relative to the ARIMA base forecasts and by `r num$suppVarVsBaseRange`% relative to the VAR base forecasts.
The relative MSEs of separate and joint reconciliation never differ by more than `r num$suppMaxSepJointDiff`.

::: {#tbl-supp-exp2}
```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(readLines(tar_read(table_supp_exp2)), sep = "\n")
```

Experiment 2: MSE of separate and joint MinT reconciliation relative to the base forecasts, averaged over 500 replications, 16 series and horizons 1--12.
:::

`\clearpage`{=latex}

# Application: ETS base forecasts {.unnumbered}

@tbl-app-accuracy-ets repeats the accuracy comparison of the main text with base forecasts from automatically selected ETS models.
For ETS we estimate the covariance matrices from response residuals, because the innovation residuals of multiplicative-error models are relative errors.

::: {#tbl-app-accuracy-ets}
```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(readLines(tar_read(table_app_ets)), sep = "\n")
```

Application: MSE relative to base forecasts (ETS), geometric mean over the series at each level, averaged over `r num$appOrigins` forecast origins (`r num$appOriginsFull` with all twelve horizons) and horizons 1--12.
:::

# Application: results by horizon {.unnumbered}

@tbl-supp-horizon-arima breaks down the comparison of joint and separate reconciliation (ARIMA base forecasts) by forecast horizon.
For admissions the ratio is above one at every horizon and level, and falls towards one as the horizon grows.
For dismissals it is below one at every horizon and level.

::: {#tbl-supp-horizon-arima}
```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(readLines(tar_read(table_supp_horizon)), sep = "\n")
```

Application (ARIMA base forecasts): MSE of joint relative to separate MinT reconciliation by forecast horizon, geometric mean over the series at each level.
:::

`\clearpage`{=latex}

# Application: results for every series {.unnumbered}

@tbl-supp-nodes gives the results series by series.
For dismissals, joint reconciliation is better than separate reconciliation for `r num$appNodesJointBetterDis`.
For admissions it is better for only `r num$appNodesJointBetterAdm`, and the differences are small.

::: {#tbl-supp-nodes}
```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(readLines(tar_read(table_supp_nodes)), sep = "\n")
```

Application (ARIMA base forecasts): MSE of separate and joint MinT reconciliation relative to the base forecasts for every series, averaged over `r num$appOrigins` origins (`r num$appOriginsFull` with all twelve horizons) and horizons 1--12.
:::
